semanticDecisions: the Facts representation (sorted unique 48-bit keys, prefix, suffix, length) is unchanged: the counting sort yields the same order as the comparison sort

below 256 keys the comparison sort stays (the counting passes' fixed cost dominates); below 8192 keys a text over a tiny alphabet (at most 8 distinct low bytes of the last unit) stays on the comparison sort, whose three-way partitioning collapses heavy duplicates faster (measured 0.6x without this fallback on a 3-letter alphabet at 2048 units)
a digit on which every key agrees is skipped: Latin-1 text sorts in three passes, BMP text in at most six
the scratch array and the 256-int histogram are transient; nothing is retained
the query-term sorts (fromExact, mergeFactKeys seams) are small and keep Arrays.sort
